fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS. Two adversarial validators read ADN (Samuels, Nov 19/20 and Nov 11/12), KTOO/Alaska Beacon (Brooks, Nov 23), Must Read Alaska (Nov 19), the AIDEA homepage recess notice, the Nov 24 continued agenda and board schedule, ADN/Mat-Su Sentinel (Bushatz, Nov 17), ADN/Alaska Beacon (Brooks, Nov 10/11) and AIDEA's July Houston op-ed. Conditions: (1) the $200M and $150M figures are the governor-elect's own statement and never 'already committed'; (2) the ANWR $175M is proposed; ADN-only figures carry PER ADN; (3) Alaska Data Corp formed in March, announced in November; (4) Ruaro rejected the idea AIDEA is rushing, never 'refused to pause'; (5) Dunleavy's 'do it right' line is from November 11th, before the pause request, never a rebuttal; (6) neither the governor-elect's statement nor the Nov 24 agenda mentions data centers, so data centers are context, never the target of the pause or a pending vote; (7) the borough letter is dated 'last week' (mid-November), never November 17th, and asks the state to reconsider; (8) more than 2,300 comments, mostly opposed; (9) 'scalable data centers' is AIDEA's July wording as reported by the Alaska Beacon, the op-ed says 'potentially, data centers'; op-ed lines are dated July; (10) 'near Houston' for the 6,800 acres; (11) lawsuit by an unnamed former state legislator, no legal theory; (12) the reassess quote is an earlier general statement, his team hasn't said whether he'd reverse the transfer; (13) a DNR answer after December 7th is our inference and is said as 'could'; (14) no source in this set says AI except the Plural CEO line in the InvestNorth launch release (the pitch, not a project); never say AIDEA's moves are AI projects; (15) no resident quotes exist, none invented.
